Regulation: B.C. Reg. 130/2026
Made under: Legislative Assembly Management Committee Act
Published in: No. 14 – B.C. Regs. 125 to 148, July 28, 2026
Deposit date: July 17, 2026

B.C. Reg. 130/2026, deposited July 17, 2026, under theLEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY MANAGEMENT COMMITTEE ACT[section 8]. Order in Council 336/2026, approved and ordered July 17, 2026. On the recommendation of the undersigned, the Lieutenant Governor, by and with the advice and consent of the Executive Council, orders that the Legislative Precinct Regulation, B.C. Reg. 274/2002, is amended as set out in the attached Schedule. — M. FARNWORTH,Minister of Transportation and Transit; J. OSBORNE,Presiding Member of the Executive Council. 1	Section 2 of the Legislative Precinct Regulation, B.C. Reg. 274/2002, is repealed and the following substituted: Limited entry, vehicular traffic and parking 2Without prior authorization of the Speaker, a person must not do any of the following: (a)	enter or remain in or on any part of the grounds where a notice, sign or information device, posted or erected by or under the authority of the Speaker, indicates that entry is prohibited or is restricted to authorized persons; (b)	enter any building or restricted area in or on the Legislative Precinct where a notice, sign or information device, posted or erected by or under the authority of the Speaker, indicates that entry is prohibited or is restricted to authorized persons; (c)	enter or remain in or on any part of the grounds that has been fenced off or enclosed; (d)	drive, operate or park a vehicle in or on the grounds where a notice, sign or information device, posted or erected by or under the authority of the Speaker, indicates that vehicle entry or parking is prohibited or is restricted to authorized persons or vehicles. 2	The following sections are added: 2.1Without prior authorization of the Speaker, a person must not block, interfere, obstruct or restrict, or attempt to block, interfere, obstruct or restrict, a person from entering on or exiting from the Legislative Precinct, including any area in a building. 3.1(1)	In this section,"activity"means an activity that impedes the responsibilities of the Speaker described in section 4 (1.1)[powers and duties of the Speaker]of the Act. (2)	Without prior authorization of the Speaker, a person must not engage in an activity in or on the Legislative Precinct where a notice, sign or information device, posted or erected by or under the authority of the Speaker, indicates that the activity is prohibited or is restricted to authorized persons. Prohibition on interfering with security systems 3.2Without prior authorization of the Speaker, a person must not interfere with a security system, including a closed-circuit television system or a closed-circuit television camera, in or on the Legislative Precinct. 3	Section 6 is repealed and the following substituted: 6(1)	A notice, sign or information device posted or erected in or on the Legislative Precinct is presumed to have been erected by or under the authority of the Speaker, unless the contrary is established. (2)	A person must not erect, remove, alter or deface any notice, sign or information device in or on the Legislative Precinct, except under the authority of the Speaker. 4	Section 8 (1) is amended by striking out "section 3, 4, 5 (1) (a) or (b) or (2), 6 or 7 (1)" and substituting "section 2, 2.1, 3, 3.1 (2), 3.2, 4, 5 (1) (a) or (b) or (2), 6 (2) or 7 (1)".

minutes_briefs.title: BC Legislative Precinct Rules Tightened: New Bans on Blocking Entry, Interfering with Security Cameras
minutes_briefs.summary: BC Regulation 130/2026 amends the Legislative Precinct Regulation (the rules for the area around the BC Legislature in Victoria). Without the Speaker's permission, people now cannot block or obstruct anyone entering or leaving the precinct, interfere with security systems such as closed-circuit TV cameras, or take part in activities that signs say are prohibited or restricted. The rules also cover driving or parking where signs prohibit it, and tampering with posted signs. These changes took effect when the regulation was deposited on July 17, 2026.
minutes_briefs.action_required: If your business operates, delivers, or holds events at or near the BC Legislative Precinct, check the posted signs and get the Speaker's authorization before entering restricted areas, parking, or running any activity there.
